nodes.summary: For every sequence of natural numbers $a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots$ with convergent denominators $q_0, q_1, q_2, \dots$ and every natural number $n$, we have $q_{n+2} = a_{n+2} q_{n+1} + q_n$.
nodes.title: Recurrence for the convergent denominators

nodes.summary: For every sequence of natural numbers $a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots$ with convergent denominators $q_0, q_1, q_2, \dots$, we have $q_1 = a_1$.
nodes.title: The convergent denominator $q_1$ equals $a_1$

nodes.summary: Let $l \ge 2$ be even and let $a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots$ be natural numbers with convergent denominators $q_0, q_1, q_2, \dots$, such that $a_i = a_{l-i}$ for $1 \le i < l$. Then $q_{l-1} \equiv a_{l/2} \, q_{l/2-1} \pmod 2$.
nodes.title: Parity of $q_{l-1}$ for a symmetric sequence, even $l$

nodes.summary: Let $l \ge 3$ be odd and let $a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots$ be natural numbers with convergent denominators $q_0, q_1, q_2, \dots$, such that $a_i = a_{l-i}$ for $1 \le i < l$. Then $q_{l-1} \equiv q_{(l-1)/2} + q_{(l-3)/2} \pmod 2$.

nodes.title: Splitting the last convergent denominator of a symmetric sequence

nodes.summary: For every sequence of natural numbers $a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots$ with convergent denominators $q_0, q_1, q_2, \dots$, we have $q_2 = a_2 a_1 + 1$.
nodes.title: The convergent denominator $q_2$ equals $a_2 a_1 + 1$

nodes.summary: For every sequence of natural numbers $a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots$ with convergent denominators $q_0, q_1, q_2, \dots$, we have $q_0 = 1$.
nodes.title: The convergent denominator $q_0$ equals $1$

nodes.summary: For a sequence of natural numbers $a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots$, its convergent denominators $q_0, q_1, q_2, \dots$ are the natural numbers defined by $q_0 = 1$, $q_1 = a_1$ and $q_{i+2} = a_{i+2} q_{i+1} + q_i$ for $i \ge 0$. They are the denominators of the convergents of $[a_0; a_1, a_2, \dots]$, and $q_i$ is the continuant $K(a_1, \dots, a_i)$; the term $a_0$ is never used.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
